channel.title: Launchpad Digital
channel.description: Florida news, briefs and getaways from Launchpad Digital, reported from primary sources.

item.title: 'Flying Cars' Fly Over Tampa Bay in Florida's First eVTOL Demonstration Flights, DeSantis Says
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: Three types of electric air taxis retraced the route of the world's first commercial airline flight, part of an FAA pilot program.

item.title: St. Johns River Floods Near Astor; Some Homes on Wildhog and Bonnet Roads Cut Off, Forecasters Say
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: Moderate flooding is happening near Astor, and minor flooding is forecast near DeLand, the National Weather Service in Melbourne says.

item.title: Personal Assistant Gets 48 Months for Stealing Nearly $10 Million From Elderly Employers, Spending It at Louis Vuitton and Gucci
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: Prosecutors say Catalina Corona cashed hundreds of checks and hid more than 300 luxury items in two storage units.

item.title: Hurricane Center Releases Its Final Report on July's Tropical Storm Bertha, Which Brought Flooding to the Panhandle Coast
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: The report calls Bertha 'a highly sheared tropical storm' that caused 'minor-to-moderate coastal flooding' on the northern Gulf Coast.

item.title: Americans' Spending Rose 0.5% in September as Prices Climbed 3.6% From a Year Earlier, BEA Says
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: Personal income rose 0.2%, and the saving rate was 3.8%. After inflation, disposable income fell 0.3%.

item.title: Syrian Hacker Who Worked for Assad's Regime Gets 42 Months; DOJ Says One Hack Briefly Erased $136 Billion in Stock Value
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: Ahmad Umar Agha hacked about 47 Western media outlets, businesses, NGOs and government entities, the Justice Department says.

item.title: DHS Says ICE Arrested 4,170 People in a 10-Day Texas Enforcement Operation
item.dc:creator: Ryan Castillo
item.description: The department says the 'Lone Star Mission' ran Oct. 19 to Oct. 29 with state and local partners.

item.title: Six Sentenced in Tampa in a Smuggling and Asylum-Fraud Scheme Behind Over 1,700 Fake Claims, DOJ Says
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: Sentences range from two to four years. Prosecutors say migrants paid $1,500 to $40,000 and some were flown in on chartered planes.

item.title: Alphabet Says Revenue Rose 25% to $127.6 Billion; Google Cloud Sales More Than Doubled
item.dc:creator: Ryan Castillo
item.description: The Google parent reported third-quarter earnings of $2.12 a share. Google Services revenue grew 11%.

item.title: NASA Asks Companies How They Could Boost, Service or Safely Bring Down the Hubble Space Telescope
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: Hubble is likely to re-enter the atmosphere around 2033 to 2034, so a mission would need to fly by 2032, NASA says. Responses are due Nov. 30.

item.title: Coastal Flooding Continues From Jacksonville to the Keys; State Warns Drivers About Saltwater
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: Warnings and advisories cover much of Florida's Atlantic coast, and rip currents stay dangerous through the weekend.

item.title: More Than 4.27 Million Floridians Have Voted Ahead of Tuesday's Election, State Data Show
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: About 2.5 million voted early in person and nearly 1.77 million returned mail ballots, according to the Division of Elections.

item.title: EU Creates an Expert Group to Prepare Europe for Wildfires and Extreme Weather, Including a Possible Firefighting Fleet
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: The 17-member PreparEU Advisory Group meets in early November and reports to Ursula von der Leyen by spring 2027.

item.title: Weather Service Warns of 'Major Saltwater Flooding' in the Florida Keys This Evening
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: A coastal flood warning covers the Upper, Middle and Lower Keys until 11 p.m. Friday. Numerous roads may close.

item.title: Midday Brief: Friday, Oct. 30, 2026
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital News Staff
item.description: Coastal flooding from Jacksonville to the Keys, 4.27 million Floridians have voted, and the rest of Friday's news, every fact linked to its source.

item.title: Sheriff's Office: Driver Rammed a Deputy's Truck, Hit a Water Pipe and Crashed Into a Tampa Apartment Building While Fleeing
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: Deputies and a K9 tracked him down on foot after Thursday morning's attempted traffic stop, the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office says. He faces five charges.

item.title: NASA Will Fly the Public's Names to Saturn's Moon Titan on Its Dragonfly Rotorcraft; Sign-Ups Close Jan. 15
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: Names go on a microchip aboard the mission, scheduled to launch in 2028 and arrive in 2034. Everyone who signs up gets a digital boarding pass.

item.title: Russia's Novaya Gazeta Says It Will Close Nov. 9, Blaming Pressure From Authorities
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: The independent newspaper, founded more than 30 years ago, says it was evicted from its Moscow office and cut off from reader donations. "We have been killed," its statement begins.

item.title: Trump Holds a Midterm Rally in Daytona Beach Tonight; Expect Road Closures Around the Ocean Center
item.dc:creator: Ryan Castillo
item.description: Doors open at 3:30 p.m. and the president is expected to speak at 7 p.m. Republican governor nominee Byron Donalds is expected to join him, four days before the Nov. 3 election.

item.title: Morning Brief: Friday, Oct. 30, 2026
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital News Staff
item.description: New Launchpad stories first, then Thursday's stories from the Evening Brief.

item.title: Special Report: Sir Patrick Stewart, From Mirfield to the Royal Shakespeare Company to the Starship Enterprise
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: A look back at the life and career of the actor who died Wednesday, drawn from his family's memorial notice, the Royal Shakespeare Company and the official U.K. honours record.

item.title: Evening Brief: Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital News Staff
item.description: New Launchpad stories since Wednesday's Evening Brief come first, then the rest of the recent coverage.

item.title: Nearly 3.9 Million Floridians Have Voted With Five Days Until the Nov. 3 Election
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: Another 376,000-plus ballots came in over a single day, the state's figures show. Early votes now top 2.2 million, and about 752,000 mail ballots are still out.

item.title: Ukrainian Man Gets 70 Months in Federal Prison in Ransomware Case Investigated by FBI Tampa
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: Artem Stryzhak pleaded guilty to two conspiracy counts. Federal prosecutors say the Hive group hit about 1,500 victims worldwide, including hospitals.

item.title: Brevard Voters Decide Nov. 3 Whether to Renew the Half-Cent Lagoon Tax for 10 More Years
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: The Save Our Indian River Lagoon sales tax voters approved in 2016 runs out Dec. 31. Here's what the ballot question says and what happens either way.

item.title: Spacewalkers Install the Space Station's Seventh Roll-Out Solar Array in a 7-Hour, 11-Minute Spacewalk
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: NASA's Anil Menon and Canada's Joshua Kutryk added the new array Thursday. One more is planned for a Nov. 5 spacewalk, which NASA says will finish the station's power upgrade.

item.title: Sir Patrick Stewart, Star Trek's Captain Picard and X-Men's Professor X, Has Died
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: His family announced on his verified X account that he died Wednesday at his Los Angeles home after "a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia."

item.title: DoorDash Agrees to Buy Instacart for About $17 Billion
item.dc:creator: Ryan Castillo
item.description: The companies say DoorDash will pay $65 a share, mostly in cash. The deal still needs approval from Instacart shareholders and regulators and isn't expected to close until late 2027 or the first half of 2028.

item.title: U.S. Economy Grew at a 3.4% Rate in the Third Quarter, First Government Estimate Shows
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: The Bureau of Economic Analysis says growth picked up from 2.2% in the spring, driven by business investment, consumer spending and government spending. Prices measured by the PCE index rose at a 2.1% annual rate in the third quarter, down from 5.0% in the second, though September prices were up 3.6% from a year earlier.

item.title: ECB President Christine Lagarde Will Step Down Feb. 7, 2027
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: The European Central Bank says Lagarde told its Governing Council and European Council President António Costa on Thursday. The European Council will appoint her successor.

item.title: Federal Public Assistance Approved for 15 Panhandle and Big Bend Counties Hit by Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: The money helps local governments and some nonprofits pay for debris removal and repairs. Help for individual households is still under federal review.

item.title: Jacksonville Sheriff's Office Releases Video and Details of Oct. 11 Police Shooting on Mar Vic Lane
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: JSO says officers shot and killed a 34-year-old woman after she fired at them. The State Attorney's Office will review the shooting, and JSO says its conclusions are still pending.

item.title: South Florida's East Coast Faces More Coastal Flooding Through the Week; Rip Current Risk Stays High
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: The National Weather Service in Miami says high tides could bring moderate flooding through at least Thursday evening, with hazardous beach and boating conditions through Thursday.

item.title: Evening Brief: Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital News Staff
item.description: New Launchpad stories since the Midday Brief come first, then developing stories and the rest of today's coverage.

item.title: Federal Reserve Holds Key Interest Rate at 3.75% to 4%; Two Policymakers Wanted a Hike
item.dc:creator: Ryan Castillo
item.description: The Fed's rate committee voted 10 to 2 to leave the federal funds rate unchanged. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented, saying they'd have raised it a quarter point. Chairman Kevin Warsh also announced a change to the committee's meeting schedule starting in 2027.

item.title: FHP Trooper Seriously Injured After Pickup Hits His Patrol Car in SR 429 Work Zone Near Bay Lake
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: The trooper was airlifted to a hospital and is in stable condition. FHP says the truck's driver failed to move over for the patrol car's emergency lights, and charges are pending.

item.title: DeSantis Awards $100 Million for 45 Springs and Water Supply Projects Across Florida
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: Half the money goes to 23 springs restoration projects and half to 22 alternative water supply projects, including $10 million for Tampa Bay Water and $12.6 million for seven Polk County communities.

item.title: U.S. Treasury Sanctions 10 People and a Russia-Based Center Over North Korean IT Worker Schemes
item.dc:creator: Claire Whitaker
item.description: Treasury says North Korean tech workers use fake identities to get hired by U.S. companies, and the regime keeps most of their pay to fund its weapons programs.

item.title: Panthers Score Three Power-Play Goals in 5-1 Win at Winnipeg
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: Carter Verhaeghe scored twice, Matthew Tkachuk had four assists and Brady Tkachuk added a goal and two assists. The two teams meet again Friday in Sunrise.

item.title: U.K. Announces £10 Billion in New Support for Ukraine, Its Largest Package Yet
item.dc:creator: Ryan Castillo
item.description: The British government says the money includes £500 million for Ukraine's air defenses this winter. It was announced alongside the U.K.'s 2026 Budget.

item.title: Florida Agencies Thank the People Behind the Badge on National First Responders Day
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: Police and sheriff's offices from Orlando to Tampa used Oct. 28 to recognize officers, deputies, dispatchers and the newest 911 call-takers.

item.title: More Than 3.5 Million Floridians Have Now Voted in the Nov. 3 General Election
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: Nearly 370,000 more ballots were cast in a single day, the state's figures show. Early votes now top 1.9 million, and about 847,000 mail ballots are still out six days before Election Day.

item.title: Midday Brief: Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital News Staff
item.description: New Launchpad stories since the Morning Brief come first, then this morning's stories, with any verified updates marked.

item.title: Florida AG Charges Kissimmee Man With 100 Felony Counts of Child Sexual Abuse Material, Sues AI Platform A2E
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: Attorney General James Uthmeier says the company behind A2E lets users make sexualized images of real Floridians, including children. He wants a court to stop it.

item.title: AG Uthmeier Says His Office Is Launching an Investigation Into a 'CCP-Controlled Corporation' Operating in Florida
item.dc:creator: Grant Holloway
item.description: The attorney general's post quoted a video about yacht maker Ferretti Group and its Fort Lauderdale property. Here's what the official records show and what Florida law says.

item.title: U.S. Treasury Sanctions Rwanda's Ministry of Defence and a Rwandan Bank Over Support for M23 Rebels
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Hart
item.description: Treasury says Rwanda's defense ministry directed troops fighting alongside the M23 armed group in eastern Congo, and that the Zigama Credit and Savings Society moved money and gold for them.

item.title: Weeki Wachee Springs: the mermaid show and a first-magnitude spring
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital
item.description: A classic Old Florida attraction in Hernando County, where mermaids perform in water that flows from a first-magnitude spring.

item.title: Apalachicola: two small state museums in an old Gulf cotton port
item.dc:creator: Launchpad Digital
item.description: A Franklin County fishing town on the Forgotten Coast, with an 1838 cotton merchant's home and a museum to the doctor who patented mechanical refrigeration.

item.title: India Sends Federal Team to Investigate a Cheetah's Death From Pellet Injuries
item.dc:creator: Maya Reyes
item.description: The 19-month-old male was born in India to a cheetah brought in under Project Cheetah, the country's effort to reintroduce the big cats.

item.title: A Horse Rider's Sharp Eyes Help New Zealand Remove 141 Invasive Plants From Ninety Mile Beach
item.dc:creator: Nathan Cole
item.description: New Zealand's Department of Conservation says one beachgoer's photos and phone call led crews to a hidden patch of sea spurge before it could spread.
